## Facts (3):
- [hazard] PSP webhooks must be verified before parsing (id: 01a1072a-49b4-7d03-b36d-a9f8cad8df10; source: shared/human)
  Verify every payment-provider (PSP) webhook before calling get_json(): compute HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request body with the secret in the `PSP_WEBHOOK_SECRET` env var, compare it with hmac.compare_digest against the `Psp-Signature` header, and reject events whose `Psp-Timestamp` header is more than 300 seconds old (replay protection). Answer a failed check with 401 via errors.problem.
- [hazard] No customer PII in logs (id: 01a1072a-6ba4-7480-990a-ab9acfdd0059; source: shared/human)
  Never log customer names, email addresses or postal addresses; log the customer id only. Our logs ship to a third-party vendor that is outside our data processing agreement.
- [hazard] Database connections in deployed environments (id: 01a1072a-c668-7d53-93a6-b01398f54dc8; source: shared/human)
  In production and staging the app never connects to Postgres directly; every connection goes through a pooler on port 6432 that the platform team manages. Locally, docker-compose exposes Postgres itself on 5432 with no pooler, so the problems below only show up after deploy. The pool is sized at 20 server connections per service, and long transactions starve checkout, so keep transactions short and never hold one open across… (truncated; full text: get the id above)

## Decisions (1):
- [decision] Large refunds need a second approver (id: 01a1072a-2dd6-7fa3-94c0-c94b417b601f; source: shared/human)
  A refund of more than 50,000 cents ($500) must not be issued directly: create it with status `pending_approval` so a second person approves it in the admin tool. Refunds up to that amount are issued immediately with status `issued`. Agreed with Finance in June 2026 after a mistaken $9k refund.

The pool is sized at 20 server connections per service, and long transactions starve checkout, so keep transactions short and never hold one open across an HTTP call to the ledger. With psycopg 3 you must connect with `prepare_threshold=None` to turn automatic prepared statements off.

Locally, docker-compose exposes Postgres itself on 5432 with no pooler, so the problems below only show up after deploy. The pool is sized at 20 server connections per service, and long transactions starve checkout, so keep transactions short and never hold one open across an HTTP call to the ledger.
